texts: boat, white hair
Write a doha about an old man at his boat whose hair has turned white and whose back is bent over the oar, who cannot recall when his youth slipped away, and whose arms no longer pull
The boat that once leapt over the water now creaks beneath a bent old rower with snow upon his head
can u do a doha on old age, with a boat in it, white hair and weak arms
My grandfather still rows his boat at dawn but his hands tremble now, and he laughs and says he only blinked and his black hair went white
white hair, bent back
Please write a Kabir-style doha about how hair turns white and the back bends and the knees fail, all before one notices, so that youth seems to vanish in the time it takes to turn around once
doha pls on getting old, hair gone white and strength going away
Strength departs like a guest who does not say goodbye, and the head is white before the heart knows it
I noticed this morning that I cannot climb the stairs without holding the rail, and my hair has gone grey at the temples; it seems like yesterday I was running up two at a time
peacock, forehead mark, old age
My grandmother used to wear a bright forehead mark and loved watching the peacock in our yard, but now her hands shake and her hair is white; she asks where her youth went
can u write a doha with a peacock and a forehead mark about getting old
The peacock spreads fewer feathers each year and the forehead mark rests on a wrinkled brow
Write a doha where an old woman still wears a forehead mark and watches a peacock dance, though her back is bent and her hair is white, and she wonders how her youth passed unnoticed
doha on getting old and weak, plz keep it simple
failing strength, white hair
Write a doha in Kabir's voice saying white hair and a bent frame are guests who arrive uninvited, that youth is gone before anyone notices, and that the proud young should look at the old and learn
The black hair turns to silver while the heart is still counting its coins of youth
my father tried to lift a bag of rice yesterday and could not, and he sat down on the step and laughed, saying when did my arms stop belonging to me
Write a doha that shows an old man at the mosque who can barely rise from his prayer, his hair white and his body bent, and who cannot remember when his youth left, though it was only a blink ago
mosque, old age
doha with a mosque in it about an old man, bent back and all
He enters the mosque with a bent back and a white beard, and the youth he once carried is lost at the entrance
Our neighbour used to run to the mosque for the first prayer and now his son has to hold his arm; all it took was a few winters

Please write a doha about a man who stands beside the river and looks at a diamond ring on a finger that has become thin and wrinkled, wondering where his strong young years went and when his hair turned white
doha with a river and a diamond about getting old, white hair and all
My mother took off her diamond ring last week because her fingers shrank, and we sat by the river, and she said she still feels sixteen inside; make a doha out of that
The river runs on, the diamond still shines, and the hand that wore it has become a map of years
river, diamond, white hair
Write a doha about how youth is gone before one notices, how the hair turns white and the knees begin to ache, and how the proud young man of yesterday is now a bent old figure leaning on a stick
old age, failing strength
At the family wedding, my uncle could not dance, and I realised he is the same man who once carried me on his shoulders for a whole fair; the years have taken his strength and I never saw it go
The wind of the years has silvered the hair and bowed the back, and only memory still stands upright
doha on youth gone and white hair and no strength left
doha with a cleric and a palace, about getting old and bent
cleric, palace, white hair
Please write a doha about a cleric who once spoke boldly in the halls of a palace, and now sits bent and white-haired on a low seat with failing strength, wondering how his youth passed so unnoticed
The palace walls remember a young and ringing voice, and the cleric now speaks in a whisper from a bent old body
My great-uncle was once a cleric who preached in a king's palace, and today he cannot hold a cup steady; he says his youth vanished while he was busy being important
seed, grey hair
I planted a seed with my grandson today and could hardly kneel down to the ground, my knees creaking; it felt like I was young just a moment ago
Write a doha in which an old man plants a seed with trembling hands and a bent back, though his hair is white and his strength is almost gone, and he wonders where his youth went so quickly
doha pls with a seed, about being old and weak
He plants a seed with hands that shake, and his white hair stirs in the same wind that once lifted his youth
Write a Kabir-like doha telling the young not to laugh at the old, for white hair and a bent back come to everyone, and that youth, which seems so long, is over before it can be properly understood
white hair, bent body
Youth runs ahead like a child, and old age walks slowly behind, white-haired and smiling, knowing it will catch up
doha on how youth ends before you notice, hair gets white
My son laughed at my slow walk today, and I smiled, remembering that I once laughed at my father in the same way; the years have turned me into him
old age
The black bees of youth have left the hair, and only a white blossom of age remains on the branch of the head
Kabir spoke of the white hair as a warning that youth has gone, and the body is getting weak, so please write a doha that looks gently at this passage from a young body to an aged one
doha about the white hair and the bent back coming on
I looked at old photographs last night and could not recognise the man with the thick black hair who looked back, and I wonder when it all slipped by
churn, bent back, old
My grandmother used to turn the churn every morning before dawn, but now she cannot grip the handle, and her hair has gone white; she says it seems like only a week ago she was strong
doha on an old woman who cant turn the churn anymore, getting weak with age
The churn once turned with a young woman's strength, and now it waits in the corner for a hand that has grown weak
Write a doha about a woman at the churn whose hair has turned white and whose back is bent, who finds her strength quietly gone, and who remembers her youth as a day that passed while she looked away
doha on sandalwood and getting old, white hair and weak limbs
Write a Kabir-style doha in which the old man grinds sandalwood paste with a trembling hand, hair white as the paste itself, and remembers his youth that passed in a day and cannot be called back
The sandalwood keeps its fragrance, but the hand that ground it has lost its strength, and the hair is white
My grandfather could still smell sandalwood from the next room, but he could no longer walk to it; he says youth ended on a Tuesday and he only noticed on Wednesday
sandalwood, white hair
tree, bent back
My grandmother sat under the same tree where she played as a girl and told me she does not know what happened to the years in between, only that her hair is white and her knees ache
doha with a tree about getting old, white hair and weak
Write a doha in which an aging tree bends low in the wind, as the old man beneath it bends his back, and both have lost the strength of their youth without noticing the day it left
The tree bends low and so does the old man beneath it, and both remember green seasons

Write a doha about a physician who treats everyone but cannot cure his own white hair and failing strength, for the years arrive for the healer as it does for the sick, and youth leaves before anyone notices
physician, old age
The physician mixes remedies for every ill, yet no herb dyes back the white from his own hair
doha with a physician in it, about growing frail and grey
Our family physician was so strong and sharp when I was a boy, and last week I saw him walk with a stick and forget a patient's name; the years do not ask permission
The stone step is worn in the middle by feet that were young once, and at the inn the old man rests his bent back
On the way to the pilgrimage we stopped at an inn, and my father sat on a stone and couldn't get up without help; he used to carry me up this same hill, and now white hair covers his head
doha with a stone and an inn, about getting old and tired

Please write a doha in which an old man rests his bent body on a stone outside an inn, with white hair and failing strength, and recalls how his youth, which felt endless, disappeared like a passing guest
stone, inn, old age
doha with a cloud and a thief about getting old, hair white, strength going
The cloud turns white and so does the hair, and the thief of years has stolen the strength from the arm
cloud, thief, white hair
My grandfather says a thief came and took his youth without a sound, and he looks at the cloud and laughs; his hair is white now
Write a doha in which time is a thief who sneaks away with the strength of the young, leaving white hair like a cloud on the head and a bent back, and nobody notices until the theft is done
Like the moth, youth is drawn to a bright flame, and by the time it turns back the wings are grey and the body is bent
moth, old age
A moth fluttered round my old uncle's reading chair, and he said he used to be that quick; now he can hardly lift his arm, and his hair is white
Write a doha where a moth flutters round the evening while an old man, hair white and back bent, watches and recalls how his own youth fluttered away just as quickly and just as unnoticed
doha with a moth about growing old and weak
aging body, white hair
I caught my reflection in a shop window and for a second did not know the stooped, white-haired man; I thought I was still twenty-five

Please write a doha about the white hair that appears before the mind has agreed to growing old, and the strength that fades before one has used it for anything worthwhile, so youth passes like a visitor
The body bends like a drying branch, and the hair whitens before the heart has said goodbye to spring
doha on how fast youth goes, hair turning white and body going weak
doha with a bee and a lotus about growing old, white hair
My grandmother sits by the lotus pond and watches a bee, and says she used to be as quick; her hair is white and her hands tremble but her eyes are young
The bee that once sipped the lotus now rests, and the white-haired watcher counts her vanished springs
Please write a doha in which a bee circles a lotus while an old woman watches from a bent back, her hair white and her strength nearly gone, and she remembers how her youth passed in a single season
bee, lotus, old age
The furnace has grown cold, the house is quiet, and the old man's white hair is the last smoke of a fierce youth
Write a doha about an old blacksmith who once kept the furnace blazing all night and now sits in the house with white hair and a bent back, unable to lift the hammer or recall when his strength went
My grandfather's furnace has been cold for ten years, and his house feels empty without the sound of it; he sits, white-haired, and says youth is something that leaves while you are busy
doha with a furnace and a house about getting old, weak and white haired
furnace, house, old age
Please write a doha where an old man drinks milk because his teeth have gone, while his parrot repeats the words of his youth; he is white haired, bent, and wondering where his strength went
The parrot still shouts the old man's youthful boasts, while he sips his milk with a trembling hand
My grandfather feeds his parrot first and then sips his milk, for he cannot chew, and he tells it stories of when he was strong; his hair is all white now
doha with milk and a parrot about getting old, no teeth, white hair
milk, parrot, old age
fish, bell, old age
Write a doha in which an old man hears the bell and sees a fish in the water, remembering how swiftly he once moved, and now with white hair he sits and wonders where his strength went
The evening bell rang and my uncle tried to hurry to the pond to feed the fish, but his legs would not obey; he stopped, grey haired and breathless, and said when did this happen
The bell rings out the hours, the fish flashes in the pond, and the white head nods, remembering a strong age
doha with a fish and a bell about getting old, white hair and weak

Please write a Kabir-style doha about an old man who sits outside under the stars at night and counts the days of his youth, remembering how quickly his black hair turned white and his strength drained away
Under the stars on the roof, my father said he could no longer see the small ones clearly, and his hair is white as the milky sky; I wonder how the years went so fast
stars, white hair
The stars are silver and so is his hair, and each has counted the long night without once being asked
doha with stars about getting old, white hair, bent and weak
tree, white hair
Write a Kabir-like doha about a tree that has lost its leaves and an old man who has lost his youth, both standing bare in the wind, both bent and weak, neither remembering the day the strength left
doha on a tree and getting old, hair white and body bent
The old tree stands in white blossom and so does the old man's head, but only one will bloom again
My aunt's old tree has dropped most of its leaves, just like her hair has turned white, and she says nobody warned her youth would be so short
The heron stands on one leg in the shallow water, and the old man stands the same way, bent and white, on his stick
doha with a heron about getting old, white hair, no strength
There is a heron by the pond and an old man on the bank who stands just as still; I realised he has white hair and a bent back, and wondered about the strong youth he must have been
heron, old age
Please write a doha in which a white heron stands on a single leg and an old man, white of hair and bent of back, stands beside it, both waiting, and both a little puzzled at how quickly youth went
The blind man and the physician both grow old, and neither can see the youth that slipped away behind them
The blind man at our corner and the physician who treats him are both white-haired, both bent, and both complain that their strength went before they noticed
doha with a blind man and a physician about getting old, weak
Write a doha where a blind man leans on his stick and a physician leans on a table, both with white hair and failing strength, and each surprised at how fast their youth went
blind man, physician, old age
The furnace was fierce at dawn and tame at dusk, and the old man's strength is the same, spent at the end
furnace, white hair
doha with a furnace about getting old, no strength left
Please write a doha about a man whose strength once fed a roaring furnace but whose body is now bent and whose hair is white, and who does not know when his youth was spent
My father ran a small workshop with a furnace, and at sixty his arms cannot lift what they once did, and his hair is white; he says it all happened in a single season
The grindstone turns slowly under the old woman's hand, grinding out the last of her strength, and her hair is as white as the flour
grindstone, old age
Write a doha in which an old woman at the grindstone tires after only a few turns, her hair white and her back bent, and wonders where the strong arms of her youth have disappeared to
My grandmother used to grind flour on the grindstone every dawn, and today she tried and could not complete a turn; she sat down and said, when did I get so old
doha with a grindstone about getting old and weak, white hair
The old man sits like a bird in a cage with white feathers, and the milk in his cup is all that he can eat
doha with a cage and milk, about getting old, white hair and weak
cage, milk, old age
My grandfather has a bird in a cage and a cup of milk each evening, and both are in a way his only company now; his hair is white and his strength has gone
Please write a doha in which an old man sits beside an empty cage with a cup of milk, his hair white and his back bent, and he wonders how his own youth flew out of him so silently
The beggar and the king grow white-haired in the same fire of years, and both warm bent hands at its ending glow
Write a doha where an old beggar warms his bent hands at a fire, his hair white and his strength gone, and he remembers how his young body once ran through the streets without tiring or pausing
beggar, fire, white hair
doha with a beggar and a fire about getting old and weak
The old beggar at our corner lights a small fire every evening and his hands shake as he holds them out; he says he was a champion wrestler once, and the years took everything
The one-string lute sings in a quavering voice now, like its old player, bent and silver-haired
Please write a doha about an old musician whose fingers tremble on the one-string lute, whose back is bent and hair white, and who remembers when his song rang loud and his youth seemed endless
one-string lute, old age
My great-uncle used to play the one-string lute at every village fair, and now his fingers are too stiff to hold it; his hair is white and he says youth went by like a song
doha with a one-string lute about getting old, white hair, weak
river, white hair
Write a Kabir-style doha in which an old man sits by the river and sees his white hair and wrinkled face in the water, bent and weak, and wonders where the strong boy who swam here went
The river keeps its youth, but the swimmer has grown white, and cannot lift his arms to its play
I took my father back to the river where he used to swim and he stood at the edge unable to enter; his hair is white and I saw it dawn on him
doha with a river about getting old, white hair and weak limbs
doha about the stars and getting old, white hair, bent back
My grandfather looked up at the stars from his chair last night and said he could no longer find the constellations he knew, his eyes weak and his hair white; the years went by unannounced
Please write a Kabir-style doha about an old man who looks at the stars from his weak and bent body, remembers how strong he was in youth, and finds his white hair is the only silver left in his life
stars, old age
The stars are old and unbent, but the watcher below has white hair and a failing back
My uncle opened his wardrobe last week and found clothes from when he was thin and strong, and none of them fit; he sat on the bed and said how fast it all went by
grey hair, weak knees
doha on getting old and weak, white hair and stuff
Write a doha about the silent arrival of age, the grey hair, the weak knees, the failing sight, so that a proud person wakes one day and finds youth has gone without a farewell
Silently as dusk steals the colour from the sky, age steals the black from the hair
bent body
Please write a doha in the voice of Kabir that says youth is a guest who leaves without notice, hair turns white and the body bends, and the proud who once ran fast must now be helped across the road
I helped my father cross the road today, and he said it is odd, I once held his hand to cross, and now he holds mine; time did that without telling either of us
doha about old age creeping up, hair white and body weak
The roads that once felt too short for young feet are now far too long for the old
snake, old age
doha with a snake about growing old, the skin gets thin, hair white
Write a doha in which a snake sheds its skin and grows new, while an old man cannot shed his wrinkles and white hair, and he wonders how his youth ended before he could know it
I found a snake skin in the garden and my grandfather said, if only we could do that; he is eighty, white-haired, and says he did not notice youth going
The snake can shed its aged skin and be young again, but man grows only whiter, only more bent
The knees creak like old doors, the hair turns the colour of frost, and the heart is still sixteen
Write a doha about the surprise of aging, how the knees begin to ache, the hair turns white, the voice gets thin, and the person inside still feels as young as ever though the body has changed
At my sixtieth birthday I tried to run for the bus and my knees refused, and the young conductor offered me a seat; it was strange, I felt like I was twenty
aching knees, white hair
doha on getting old, hair white, knees weak, heart still young
At the pond a heron stood near my grandfather, and both stood thin and still and white-haired; he said, we are the same, we wait and we do not move, and I wanted a doha for him
The heron and the old man stand by the same pond, and both have lost the swiftness of their days
doha with a heron about being old and white haired and weak
Please write a doha in which a heron stands patient and still at the edge of a pond beside an aged man, whose hair is as white as the bird's feathers, and both wait while their youth drifts away
heron, white hair
thief, old age
Write a doha about how the thief called age steals youth, strength and beauty one by one, leaving the white hair and the bent back as signs of what is gone, without the owner ever raising an alarm
My neighbour was robbed last night of a few rupees, but I was thinking of my father who is losing his memory and his strength; that thief takes more, and nobody gets it back
Age is a thief who walks in softly, takes the black from the hair, and leaves only silver
doha with a thief in it about getting old, white hair and no strength
doha with a cuckoo about getting old, voice cracks, hair white
The cuckoo's song is sweet in spring, but the old man's voice has become a whisper among white branches
My grandmother used to sing like a cuckoo, and now her voice is thin and her hair is all white; she says youth went when she was busy loving us
Please write a doha in which a cuckoo sings in the spring while an old man hears it with a bent back and white hair, remembering the clear voice and the strong body of his own youth
cuckoo, old age
sun, white hair
The old man sits in the sun every morning because his bones feel cold even in summer, and his hair is white as snow; he says youth was over before he had even thanked it
Write a doha in which a bent and white-haired old man warms himself in the sun that once he walked under with strong steps, and wonders in silence how his young years ever went so fast
The sun rises as young as ever on a head that has grown white and a back that has grown low
doha with the sun about getting old and weak, white hair
Write a doha in which an old man sits beside a snake charmer's basket and sees a bier pass, his hair white and his body bent, and wonders how quickly his youth went and how soon he follows
snake, bier, old age
The snake sleeps in its basket, the bier moves down the lane, and the old watch with tired eyes
doha with a snake and a bier about growing frail, hair white, strength gone
At the funeral my grandfather watched the bier go by and a snake curled by the roadside, and he told me that he too is white haired and weak and will be next
The leaf yellows and falls in the same wind that whitens the hair, and the pot of water on the shelf waits for a hand that trembles
Write a doha in which an old man lifts a pot of water with trembling hands and sees a leaf float on top, and he realises his strength is gone like the green of that leaf
My grandmother could not lift the pot of water this morning and a leaf from the neem fell into it as she tried; she looked at me and said, I am old now, aren't I
doha with a pot of water and a leaf about getting old, weak hands, white hair
pot of water, leaf, aging
The rope of the years is frayed, the lamp of the eyes burns low, and the white head nods toward the dark
My father's hands have gone so weak that he can't tie the rope on the cow anymore, and the lamp by his bed burns all night; he says his youth went when he wasn't looking
doha with a rope and a lamp about getting old, white hair and weak
Write a doha in which an old man tries to knot a rope with weak hands by a lamp, his hair white and his back bent, and he remembers when the same hands could pull a bull
rope, lamp, old age
At the crossroads the old man stands white as ash, bent and slow, and the young pass him like leaves in the wind
I stood with my father at the crossroads waiting to cross, and the young ones rushed past; he said, I used to rush too, and his hair looked like ash
doha with a crossroads and ash about old age, white hair, weak legs
Write a doha in which an old man stands at a crossroads, his hair as white as ash, his back bent, and his strength gone, and the young hurry past him without noticing that they will be here next
crossroads, ash, white hair
swan, old age
There is a swan on the pond near my grandfather, and he says they look alike now, white and slow and a little bent; he laughs but his eyes are wistful
The swan glides, white and slow, and the old man beside the pond is white and slow too, but only one can still rise
doha with a swan about getting old, white hair, bent back
Please write a doha in which a white swan floats serenely on the water and an old man with white hair and a bent back watches it, remembering his own strong youth that vanished without a goodbye
one-string lute, white hair

Write a Kabir-style doha in which an old singer plays the one-string lute with fingers that no longer obey, his hair white and his voice thin, and he wonders at the speed with which the strength of youth left him
The one-string lute and the old singer have both lost their sweetness, strings loose and voice thin
My grandfather has put away his one-string lute because his fingers hurt, and his hair has gone white; he says he did not hear his youth go
doha with a one-string lute about getting old and weak, white hair
doha on getting old, can't walk fast anymore, hair white
old age, weak knees
The long road of the years narrows to a short lane, and the walker's hair is silver

Please write a Kabir-style doha about the quiet moment when a person realises their hair has turned white, their strength has faded and their youth is over, and that no one warned them it would be so short
My mother used to run up the stairs two at a time and now takes ten minutes to climb them, holding the rail and laughing about it; her hair is white and her hands are thin

A thief broke into our neighbour's home while he slept on the sand-coloured quilt and he did not hear it; the old man is so deaf and white-haired now, and he says even his youth was stolen the same way
thief, sand, old age
doha with a thief and sand about getting old, hair white
Write a doha in which a thief called age steals youth grain by grain like sand, leaving an old man with white hair and a bent back who sits and asks himself where all those years went
Youth runs through the fingers like sand, and the thief of years takes the rest, leaving only the white of the head
